chs-great-bras-dor.name: Great Bras d'Or
chs-great-bras-dor.source: The sea entrance to the Bras d'Or Lakes; the rapid is at the outer narrows between Carey Point and Noir Point, not at the Seal Island Bridge 4.7 miles southwest. Sailing Directions ATL 104 refers the mariner to the current tables for slack water here. CHS names the same station both "Big Bras D'Or" and "Great Bras D'or"; the channel is Great Bras d'Or, so that is the name, with the other carried as an alias. Position from CHS's public current-station list, matched by position and confirmed in the channel - the tide reference ports' method, see PROVENANCE.md. Note for a consumer: slack here lags high and low water by hours - a 3.5 to 4 h median across the 2026 predictions, ranging 2.5 to 5.5 - and the stream direction is inverted relative to the sea tide, flowing out while the tide rises. Slack must never be derived from tide height; read the current table.

chs-masset-sound.name: Masset Sound
chs-masset-sound.source: The long sound on north Graham Island joining Masset Inlet to Dixon Entrance, pinching to under two cables at Cook Point, which Sailing Directions says should be navigated at or near slack water - slack lasting only a few minutes. The 2026 predictions peak at 5.8 knots ebbing and 5.6 flooding, with a median peak nearer 3.8 either way. Named for the sound, as the Sailing Directions and tide tables name it; CHS's station file says "Masset Channel", carried as an alias. Cited to PAC 206 when this entry was written; that volume is superseded by PAC 203, which carries the same wording. Position from CHS's public current-station list, matched by position and confirmed in the sound - the tide reference ports' method, see PROVENANCE.md.

chs-nakwakto-rapids.name: Nakwakto Rapids
chs-nakwakto-rapids.source: The sole entrance to the Seymour and Belize Inlet complex, at the east end of Slingsby Channel around Bramham Island, with Turret Rock mid-channel. Sailing Directions PAC 202 is unusually direct about the timing: slack runs about six minutes, and it says the rapids cannot be run safely at any other time. The ebb is the faster stream - CHS gives 14.5 knots ebbing against 11.5 flooding. Position from CHS's public current-station list, matched by position and confirmed in the channel - the tide reference ports' method, see PROVENANCE.md.

chs-quatsino-narrows.name: Quatsino Narrows
chs-quatsino-narrows.source: The mile-and-a-half narrows east of Drake Island joining Quatsino Sound to Holberg and Rupert Inlets, on northwest Vancouver Island. The Pacific Pilotage Authority gates even piloted ships through it on daylight slack. The transit outlasts the slack, so a consumer states the turn, not a window. Position from CHS's public current-station list - the tide reference ports' method, see PROVENANCE.md - held at the published latitude and moved ~170 m west to mid-channel: the published longitude (-127.5550) lands on the islet between the two threads of the narrows, and the on-land audit caught it. Same treatment as chs-malibu-rapids, and the reason the audit is a failure rather than a note.

noaa-boundary-pass.name: Boundary Pass
noaa-boundary-pass.source: NOAA CO-OPS station; position from the NOAA station page, not the CHS fitting pipeline that supplies the other gates. See PROVENANCE.md.

chs-malibu-rapids.name: Malibu Rapids
chs-malibu-rapids.source: No CHS current station; slack is derived from Point Atkinson high/low water (HW+25 / LW+35 min, cruising-community consensus - Points North seminar, Waggoner). Position is in the Malibu Rapids channel on the Jervis Inlet approach, nudged ~110 m off the CHS Malibu Islet station (50.163, -123.85), which sits sub-resolution on the bundled coastline. See PROVENANCE.md.
